title: Binding Multiple Modalities via Multimodal Wasserstein Barycenter
claim: Aligning all modalities around a learned shared barycenter anchor, rather than one bound modality, yields more balanced retrieval and generation.
layout: 2 panels: left sphere-geometry schematic, right bar chart plus image grid
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a), 'Core idea', shows a translucent sphere with three modality distributions at the edge: Video P2 (green), Audio P1 (blue) and Text Pk (orange). Dashed arrows labeled W(P, Q) point from each distribution to a pink central cluster Q, the Wasserstein barycenter. A pink arrow labeled WB leads to a second hemisphere, where the 'WB embedding' sits at the apex of a barycenter simplex. Colored dashed edges connect it to text, audio and video points, with 'Volume Contrasting' written beside it. Yellow and pink rounded boxes name the two stages. Panel (b), 'Examples', shows a grouped bar chart of T2V and V2T Recall@1 for VAST-1B, BaryBind-1B and InternVideo2-6B, with gap annotations (Δ=5.6%, 2.5%, 5.8%). Next to it is a 2x3 grid of generated images (ImageBind, GRAM, BaryBind) for text+audio prompts. The eye goes first to the sphere on the left.
caption: BaryBind learns the multimodal Wasserstein Barycenter (WB) of all modalities via WB optimization, and the WB serves as the anchor to bind modalities via volumetric alignment based on the barycenter simplex volume. Notably, BaryBind yields more balanced multimodal retrieval results and enables TA2I generation that well preserves both text and audio semantics.
abstract: Multimodal learning beyond two modalities commonly leverages a specific modality (e.g., text) to bind other modalities. However, how to establish a more balanced representation space that approximates shared semantics while respecting the holistic geometry of $n$-modal data remains challenging. In this work, we present BaryBind, which aims to transport the specific modality towards the Wasserstein barycenter (WB) optimized across all modalities and introduces a volumetric alignment objective to establish a unified semantic space around the WB embedding. Specifically, we project specific modalities to the WB, which minimizes the average Wasserstein distances to multimodal distributions and serves as the anchor for subsequent alignment. We then construct a barycenter simplex, whose volume is taken as a similarity metric for global alignment centered at the WB. Experiments show that BaryBind achieves competitive performance in text-video-audio retrieval, classification, videoQA, and cross-modal generation tasks, along with robustness under modality absence and scalability to more than three modalities. Code is released at https://github.com/xl-tang3/BaryBind.
